cases.name: bad-undeclared-helper
cases.why: A helper reachable from the fixture's /cpp:init writes $HOME/.claude/fixture and carries no declaration. This is the drift the seam exists to make visible: a surface a consumer's defer-set cannot name because CPP never declared it.

cases.name: good-all-declared
cases.why: Byte-identical to the bad case except the helper declares the surface it writes. The pair isolates the declaration as the only difference, so a green cannot come from the fixture being trivially empty.

_comment: Registration for scripts/host-surface-check.py (issue #1139).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets work
THROUGH, and its green is consumed OUTSIDE this repository. A managed
environment reads the manifest this gate validates and sizes its own defer-set
and drift coverage against it; nothing downstream re-derives which helpers were
supposed to declare. A blind version here hands a consumer a short list that
looks complete, and the consumer then fences the surfaces it knows about while
CPP writes one it does not.
THE CASES ARE WHOLE FIXTURE TREES, not the real repository. The gate takes
--root, so a case is a miniature repo: a `.claude/commands/cpp/` with two
command documents and a one-line `scripts/` helper they invoke.
THE PAIR IS BYTE-IDENTICAL EXCEPT FOR THE DECLARATION LINE. Both fixtures
contain the same helper writing the same $HOME path from the same fenced
invocation; only the `#: HOST-SURFACE:` line differs. So a green on the good
case cannot come from the fixture being trivially empty, and the bad case
cannot score BAD for an incidental second reason.
WHAT THIS CONTROL DOES NOT PROVE, stated because the gate's own verdict says
so: it exercises the MISSING-DECLARATION direction only. A declaring helper
that UNDERSTATES its surfaces is not detectable by this gate at all - that
needs observation, not parsing - so no case here can exercise it, and its
absence is a bound rather than a gap in coverage.
Stdlib-only and git-free, like the gate: nothing this fixture needs is absent
from the slim CI image, so the control gives the same verdict there as here.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new and never shipped blind, so there is no revision to vendor - `--verify-provenance` therefore reports `unverified`, which is correct and must never be read as `ok`. This is the FIRST FRAMING and the one #1139 was filed against: a HAND-MAINTAINED list of helpers believed to write host surfaces. #1132's table named five, a doc-grep suggested fourteen, a wider grep thirty-eight - each a hardcoded membership. The single difference from the real gate is that membership is a constant here and derived from reachability there; the declaration syntax, verdict lines and exit codes are identical, so the demonstration isolates the derivation. It MISSES bad-undeclared-helper because the fixture's helper is not on the list, which is precisely how a hand-maintained list fails in production, and it AGREES on good-all-declared, which keeps the demonstration isolated rather than a blanket disagreement.
